errors.text_span: The chart is divided into three distinct segments
errors.evidence: The chart has two rings (inner and outer), not three segments. The description incorrectly conflates the two rings into a single pie with three segments.

errors.text_span: the largest segment, colored light blue, represents “Clear” conversations and accounts for 47.7% of the samples; the medium-sized segment, in medium blue, corresponds to “Somewhat ambiguous” conversations at 38.0%; and the smallest segment, in dark blue, indicates “Very ambiguous” conversations, making up 14.2% of the total
errors.evidence: The description incorrectly maps colors and labels to categories. The 47.7% segment corresponds to 'Max: 1' (inner ring, medium blue), 38.0% corresponds to 'Std: 0.47' (outer ring, medium blue), and 14.2% corresponds to 'Max: 3' (inner ring, very light blue). The description also invents category names ('Clear', 'Somewhat ambiguous', 'Very ambiguous') that do not exist in the figure.

errors.text_span: the smallest segment, in dark blue, indicates “Very ambiguous” conversations, making up 14.2% of the total
errors.evidence: The 14.2% segment is in very light blue (inner ring, 'Max: 3'), not dark blue. The dark blue segment (outer ring, 'Std: 0.0') accounts for 49.0%, not 14.2%.
The description does not explicitly state that the chart shows two distinct sets of data: 'Ambiguity Std' (outer ring) and 'Max Ambiguity' (inner ring).
The description omits the outer ring entirely, which includes four categories: 'Std: 0.0' (49.0%), 'Std: 0.47' (38.0%), 'Std: 0.82' (5.0%), and 'Std: 0.94' (7.0%).
The description does not mention the legend, which is critical for interpreting the colors and categories in both rings.
The description does not explicitly state that the segments are arranged in descending order of size within each ring.
